content: The British School of Osteopathy (BSO) is recognized as the largest and oldest institution dedicated to the study and practice of osteopathy in the United Kingdom. It holds Recognised Qualification (RQ) status, which is granted by the General Osteopathic Council, the statutory regulatory body for osteopathy in the UK. The BSO was established in 1915, although its formal incorporation was delayed until 1917 due to the impact of the First World War. The institution was granted charity status in 1963. In 1984, HRH The Princess Royal became the official Patron of the school. Since 2005, the University of Bedfordshire has been responsible for validating the BSO’s four-year degree programs. Students enrolled in the BSO’s osteopathy programs are eligible to apply for government and European Union funding to cover tuition fees. As part of their training, students gain hands-on clinical experience by treating members of the public at the school’s clinics. These treatments are conducted under the supervision of fully qualified and practicing osteopaths who serve as tutors. The fees for treatment at the school’s clinics are heavily subsidized. Pensioners and individuals receiving state benefits are entitled to a 50% discount on treatment fees, and some patients are even eligible to receive treatment free of charge.
